title: Luke Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Luke 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The parable of the fig tree
Jesus healing a woman on the sabbath
The Galilaeans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices
The tower in Siloam falling and killing eighteen people
questions.correctAnswer: The Galilaeans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices
questions.explanation: Luke 13:1 mentions the Galilaeans and Pilate first in the chapter before any other events.

questions.question: Who mingled the blood of the Galilaeans with their sacrifices according to Luke 13?
questions.correctAnswer: Pilate
questions.explanation: Luke 13:1 states that Pilate mingled the blood of the Galilaeans with their sacrifices.

questions.question: What was Jesus' answer when asked if the Galilaeans were sinners above all others because they suffered?
options: Yes, they were the greatest sinners
No, but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish
Yes, and they deserved their fate
questions.correctAnswer: No, but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish
questions.explanation: Luke 13:2-3 records Jesus' answer denying they were sinners above all others and emphasizing repentance.

questions.question: What happened to the eighteen people mentioned in Luke 13?
options: They were killed by the tower in Siloam falling
They were drowned in the river
questions.correctAnswer: They were killed by the tower in Siloam falling
questions.explanation: Luke 13:4 states that the tower in Siloam fell and killed eighteen people.

questions.question: How many years had the man sought fruit on the fig tree in the parable?
questions.correctAnswer: Three years
questions.explanation: Luke 13:7 says the man had sought fruit for three years but found none.

questions.question: What did the owner want to do with the fig tree that bore no fruit?
questions.correctAnswer: Cut it down
questions.explanation: Luke 13:7 states the owner said, 'cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?'

questions.question: What did the dresser of the vineyard ask the owner to do regarding the fig tree?
options: Let it alone this year and dig about it and dung it
Graft it onto a different tree
questions.correctAnswer: Let it alone this year and dig about it and dung it
questions.explanation: Luke 13:8 records the dresser asking to delay cutting the fig tree and to dig and dung it.

questions.question: Where was Jesus teaching when he healed the woman?
questions.correctAnswer: In one of the synagogues
questions.explanation: Luke 13:10 states Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

questions.question: How long had the woman with the spirit of infirmity been afflicted?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighteen years
questions.explanation: Luke 13:11 explains the woman had been bowed together and infirm for eighteen years.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the woman when he healed her?
options: Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity
questions.correctAnswer: Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity
questions.explanation: Luke 13:12 records Jesus saying, 'Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.'

questions.question: According to Jesus, what must happen to avoid perishing, as mentioned twice in these verses?
questions.correctAnswer: Repent
questions.explanation: Luke 13:3 and 13:5 both say 'except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus taught in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 13:10 says Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

questions.question: True or False: The woman healed by Jesus was unable to lift herself up before being healed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 13:11 states she 'could in no wise lift up herself' before Jesus healed her.

questions.question: True or False: The text says the fig tree bore fruit every year.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 13:6-7 says the fig tree was sought for fruit for three years but found none.

questions.question: True or False: The text states Jesus commanded the woman to leave immediately after healing her.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 13:12 records Jesus saying she was loosed from infirmity but does not mention commanding her to leave immediately.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the immediate result when Jesus laid his hands on the woman who had been bowed together for eighteen years?
options: She was made straight and glorified God
She was given a vision of the kingdom of God
She fell asleep and dreamed of salvation
She was asked to come back the next day
questions.correctAnswer: She was made straight and glorified God
questions.explanation: Luke 13:13 states that immediately she was made straight and glorified God after Jesus laid his hands on her.

questions.question: What does Luke 13:17 promise will happen if someone recognizes the glorious things done by Jesus as stated in Luke 13:16?
options: They will become rulers of synagogues
questions.correctAnswer: All the people will rejoice
questions.explanation: Luke 13:17 says that after Jesus spoke about the woman being loosed on the sabbath (verse 16), all his adversaries were ashamed and the people rejoiced for all the glorious things done by him.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the ruler of the synagogue's indignation about healing on the sabbath?
options: He called him a hypocrite and gave examples of doing good on the sabbath
He agreed and stopped healing on the sabbath
He ignored him and continued healing silently
He told him to leave the synagogue
questions.correctAnswer: He called him a hypocrite and gave examples of doing good on the sabbath
questions.explanation: Luke 13:15 shows Jesus calling the ruler a hypocrite and pointing out that people loosen their animals to give them water on the sabbath.

questions.question: What two illustrations does Jesus give to describe the kingdom of God in Luke 13:19 and Luke 13:21?
options: A mustard seed growing into a great tree and leaven hidden in meal
A pearl of great price and a lost sheep
A sower sowing seeds and a shepherd tending sheep
A lamp on a stand and a vine with branches
questions.correctAnswer: A mustard seed growing into a great tree and leaven hidden in meal
questions.explanation: Luke 13:19 and 13:21 describe the kingdom of God as like a mustard seed that grows into a tree and like leaven hidden in three measures of meal.

questions.question: Why does Jesus say it is right to heal the woman on the sabbath?
options: Because she is a daughter of Abraham and has been bound by Satan for eighteen years
Because healing is more important than the sabbath law
Because the ruler of the synagogue requested it
Because the woman promised to follow Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Because she is a daughter of Abraham and has been bound by Satan for eighteen years
questions.explanation: Luke 13:16 explains that the woman is a daughter of Abraham and has been bound by Satan for eighteen years, so it is right to free her on the sabbath.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith and patience can be drawn from the parable of the fig tree in Luke 13:6-9?
options: God gives us time and care to bear fruit before judging
We must immediately cut off unfruitful people
Fruitfulness is irrelevant to God's kingdom
We should stop caring for those who don't improve
questions.correctAnswer: God gives us time and care to bear fruit before judging
questions.explanation: Luke 13:8-9 shows the man asking to wait another year to care for the fig tree, teaching patience and opportunity for repentance and fruitfulness.

questions.question: What does Jesus mean by saying 'Strive to enter in at the strait gate' in Luke 13:24?
options: Make earnest effort to enter the kingdom of God because it is difficult
Avoid entering any gates that are narrow
Only the rich can enter the kingdom
The gate is wide and easy to enter
questions.correctAnswer: Make earnest effort to enter the kingdom of God because it is difficult
questions.explanation: Luke 13:24 encourages believers to strive to enter the narrow gate, implying that entering the kingdom requires effort and commitment.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Luke 13:14-15, what everyday activity on the sabbath justifies doing good, such as healing?
options: Loosing oxen or asses from the stall to give them water
questions.correctAnswer: Loosing oxen or asses from the stall to give them water
questions.explanation: Luke 13:15 shows Jesus pointing out that even on the sabbath, people lead their animals to water, justifying acts of mercy like healing.

questions.question: What is the reaction of Jesus' adversaries after he defends healing on the sabbath in Luke 13:17?
questions.correctAnswer: They were ashamed
questions.explanation: Luke 13:17 states that after Jesus' defense, all his adversaries were ashamed and the people rejoiced.

questions.question: How does Jesus describe the growth of the kingdom of God in the parable of the mustard seed?
options: It starts small but grows into a great tree where birds can lodge
It is planted only in the desert
It grows slowly but never becomes visible
questions.correctAnswer: It starts small but grows into a great tree where birds can lodge
questions.explanation: Luke 13:19 describes the mustard seed growing into a great tree providing shelter for birds, symbolizing the kingdom's expansive growth.

questions.question: What does Jesus teach about the scope of salvation in Luke 13:23-24?
options: Many will seek to enter but few will be able to
Everyone will be saved without effort
Only the rich and powerful will be saved
Salvation is guaranteed to all who hear the gospel
questions.correctAnswer: Many will seek to enter but few will be able to
questions.explanation: Luke 13:24 warns that many will try to enter the kingdom but only those who strive will succeed.

questions.question: Why does Jesus refer to the woman as a 'daughter of Abraham' in Luke 13:16?
options: To emphasize her rightful place in God's covenant and deserving of healing
To show she was a biological daughter of Abraham
To indicate she was not a Jew
questions.correctAnswer: To emphasize her rightful place in God's covenant and deserving of healing
questions.explanation: Luke 13:16 highlights her identity as a daughter of Abraham to justify her healing on the sabbath as part of God's covenant people.

questions.question: What does the parable of the leaven in Luke 13:21 symbolize about the kingdom of God?
options: It spreads and transforms everything quietly and thoroughly
It is visible only at the beginning
It remains in small circles without influence
It is rejected by most people
questions.correctAnswer: It spreads and transforms everything quietly and thoroughly
questions.explanation: Luke 13:21 uses the leaven hidden in meal to illustrate the kingdom's pervasive and transformative influence.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath when he healed the woman bowed together.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 13:10 confirms Jesus was teaching in a synagogue on the sabbath when he healed the woman.

questions.question: True or False: The ruler of the synagogue appreciated Jesus' healing on the sabbath and encouraged the people to come for healing on that day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 13:14 shows the ruler was indignant and opposed Jesus healing on the sabbath.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Luke 13:25, what does the master of the house do when he rises up?
questions.correctAnswer: He shuts the door
questions.explanation: Luke 13:25 states that when the master of the house is risen up, he hath shut to the door.

questions.question: According to Luke 13:26, what do the people begin to say when they stand outside and knock?
options: We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets
questions.correctAnswer: We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets
questions.explanation: Luke 13:26 records the words of those outside as, 'We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.'

questions.question: In Luke 13:27, how does the master of the house respond to those knocking and claiming familiarity?
options: I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: Luke 13:27 explicitly states the master says, 'I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.'

questions.question: What imagery is used in Luke 13:28 to describe the fate of those thrust out of the kingdom of God?
questions.correctAnswer: Weeping and gnashing of teeth
questions.explanation: Luke 13:28 uses the vivid imagery of 'weeping and gnashing of teeth' to describe the anguish of those excluded from the kingdom.

questions.question: According to Luke 13:29, from which directions will people come to sit down in the kingdom of God?
options: From the sea and the desert
questions.correctAnswer: East, West, North, and South
questions.explanation: Luke 13:29 states that people shall come 'from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south' to sit in the kingdom of God.

questions.question: What paradoxical statement does Jesus make in Luke 13:30 about the status of the last and the first?
options: There are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last
The strong shall inherit the earth
The meek shall inherit the earth
questions.correctAnswer: There are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last
questions.explanation: Luke 13:30 contains this famous paradoxical reversal about the rankings in the kingdom of God.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'gnashing' (δακτυλισμός, daktulismos) in Luke 13:28 mean?
options: Grinding of teeth in anger or pain
questions.correctAnswer: Grinding of teeth in anger or pain
questions.explanation: The Greek term translated as 'gnashing' in Luke 13:28 refers to the grinding or clenching of teeth, typically expressing extreme anguish or anger.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in Luke 13:25-28 where the master shuts the door and denies knowing those outside?
questions.correctAnswer: Parable
questions.explanation: Luke 13:25-28 is a parabolic teaching using the story of a master shutting the door to illustrate judgment and exclusion from the kingdom.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the lament and rejection of prophets like in Luke 13:34?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 7:25
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 7:25 laments how the people have not hearkened to the prophets sent to them, paralleling Jesus' lament in Luke 13:34.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse fulfills the theme of 'Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord' found in Luke 13:35?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 21:9
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:9 records the crowd shouting 'Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord!' fulfilling the theme in Luke 13:35.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the parable of the fig tree in Luke 13?
options: Jesus speaking about repentance after reporting the Galileans’ deaths
Jesus healing the woman with infirmity
Jesus teaching about the mustard seed
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus speaking about repentance after reporting the Galileans’ deaths
questions.explanation: Luke 13:1-5 precedes the fig tree parable with Jesus addressing the need for repentance after mentioning the Galileans slain by Pilate.

questions.question: Which literary device is utilized in Luke 13:30 with the phrase 'there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last'?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Luke 13:30 employs chiasmus, a literary device where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order to emphasize contrast.

questions.question: How does Jesus typologically refer to himself in Luke 13:32 when calling Herod 'that fox'?
options: As a wise and cunning adversary to Herod's craftiness
As a wild animal to be hunted
As a shepherd of the people
questions.correctAnswer: As a wise and cunning adversary to Herod's craftiness
questions.explanation: In Luke 13:32, Jesus uses the term 'fox' metaphorically to denote Herod's cunning and craftiness, positioning himself as a resolute adversary.

questions.question: What cultural practice does Jesus reference in Luke 13:34 to illustrate His desire to protect Jerusalem?
options: A hen gathering her brood under her wings
A king sitting on a throne
questions.correctAnswer: A hen gathering her brood under her wings
questions.explanation: Luke 13:34 uses the metaphor of a hen gathering her chicks under her wings, a cultural image of protection and care in Jewish tradition.

questions.question: True or False: In Luke 13:35, Jesus predicts that the people will not see Him again until they say, 'Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 13:35 explicitly states Jesus will not be seen until the time when people say, 'Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.'

theological.title: Luke Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 13:3 teach about human sin and repentance?
options: All must repent or they will perish
Only the worst sinners need to repent
Suffering is evidence of special sinfulness
questions.correctAnswer: All must repent or they will perish
questions.explanation: Luke 13:3 states, 'except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish,' teaching the necessity of repentance for all to avoid perishing.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 13:6-9 teach about God's patience in sanctification?
options: God allows time for repentance and fruitfulness
God's patience means fruitfulness is unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: God allows time for repentance and fruitfulness
questions.explanation: Luke 13:7-9 shows the vineyard owner delaying judgment to give the fig tree one more year to bear fruit, indicating God's longsuffering patience in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and mercy is taught in Luke 13:28-29?
options: The kingdom is inclusive of all nations, but excludes unrepentant sinners
Only ethnic Israelites will enter the kingdom
Entrance to the kingdom is based on ethnic heritage alone
The kingdom is exclusively for the righteous Jews
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom is inclusive of all nations, but excludes unrepentant sinners
questions.explanation: Luke 13:28-29 describes people from all directions sitting in the kingdom, while some are cast out, emphasizing God's just mercy extended to all nations, not just Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 13:34 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Luke 13:34 shows Jesus lamenting Jerusalem's rejection despite His repeated calls, demonstrating God's longsuffering patience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by Jesus’ authority over the spirit of infirmity in Luke 13:12-13?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Luke 13:12-13, Jesus commands the spirit of infirmity to leave, immediately healing the woman, demonstrating His sovereign power over evil and sickness.

questions.question: How does Luke 13:24-27 connect to the broader biblical theme of final judgment?
options: It emphasizes the necessity of entering through the narrow gate
It teaches that all who call Jesus Lord will be saved
It endorses universal salvation regardless of works
It denies any future separation of people at judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the necessity of entering through the narrow gate
questions.explanation: Luke 13:24-27 warns that many will seek but fail to enter the kingdom, underscoring the biblical theme of final judgment and the necessity of the narrow gate.

questions.question: In what way does Luke 13:19's mustard seed parable prepare for the growth of the church in Acts?
options: It symbolizes the kingdom's small beginnings and expansive growth
It predicts the destruction of the Jewish temple
It describes the end of the world
It illustrates the immediate triumph of the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the kingdom's small beginnings and expansive growth
questions.explanation: Luke 13:19's mustard seed parable portrays the kingdom starting small and growing large, prefiguring the church's expansion in Acts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 13:3 and Luke 13:5 teach about repentance and judgment?
options: Repentance is universally required to avoid perishing
Only some need to repent for judgment to be avoided
Suffering is the proof of sinfulness
Judgment can be escaped without repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance is universally required to avoid perishing
questions.explanation: Both Luke 13:3 and 13:5 repeat that without repentance all will perish, emphasizing universal need for repentance before judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 13:14 and Luke 13:16 teach about the Sabbath and God's purpose in healing?
options: The Sabbath is intended for mercy and liberation from bondage
Healing on the Sabbath is unlawful in all cases
The Sabbath requires strict rest without exceptions
Physical healing is less important than ritual observance
questions.correctAnswer: The Sabbath is intended for mercy and liberation from bondage
questions.explanation: Luke 13:14-16 shows Jesus arguing that healing a woman bound by Satan on the Sabbath fulfills God's merciful purpose, not violating the Sabbath rest.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about the kingdom of God is taught in Luke 13:20-21 and Luke 13:18-19?
options: The kingdom grows from small beginnings to pervasive influence
The kingdom is a political dominion to be seized by force
The kingdom is exclusively for a chosen ethnic group
The kingdom will immediately eradicate all evil
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom grows from small beginnings to pervasive influence
questions.explanation: Luke 13:18-21 uses the mustard seed and leaven parables to teach that the kingdom of God starts small but grows extensively and influences all.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Luke 13:24-27 teaches that salvation can be earned by works. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Many will attempt to enter the kingdom, but only those who genuinely enter through the narrow gate will be saved
Everyone who tries will be saved regardless of their deeds
Salvation is guaranteed by mere profession of faith
The passage teaches that works alone save without faith
questions.correctAnswer: Many will attempt to enter the kingdom, but only those who genuinely enter through the narrow gate will be saved
questions.explanation: Luke 13:24-27 warns that many will seek to enter but be denied, emphasizing genuine entrance through the narrow gate rather than mere effort or works.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic mission and divine sovereignty is taught in Luke 13:33?
options: A prophet cannot perish outside Jerusalem, indicating God's sovereign plan
Prophets have freedom to avoid danger at will
Prophetic ministry is optional and not determined by God
God abandons prophets to human enemies
questions.correctAnswer: A prophet cannot perish outside Jerusalem, indicating God's sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Luke 13:33 affirms that a prophet must die in Jerusalem, showing God's sovereign control over prophetic mission and fulfillment of destiny.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by Jesus’ response to the ruler of the synagogue in Luke 13:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Jesus’ rebuke in Luke 13:15 highlights mercy over legalism, showing God's merciful desire to heal even on the Sabbath.

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by Jesus’ lament in Luke 13:34 regarding Jerusalem's rejection of the prophets?
options: God desires to gather and protect His people but respects their rejection
God is indifferent to human response
Divine judgment occurs without prior warning
God forces salvation on those who reject Him
questions.correctAnswer: God desires to gather and protect His people but respects their rejection
questions.explanation: Luke 13:34 reveals God's earnest desire to protect Jerusalem’s people, yet their rejection results in desolation, showing God's respect for human free will.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about salvation and eschatological reversal is taught in Luke 13:30 and Luke 13:29?
options: God’s kingdom reverses human expectations, including status and entrance from all nations
The first-born Israelites will always have priority
Salvation is based on social rank
Only Jews will be first in the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: God’s kingdom reverses human expectations, including status and entrance from all nations
questions.explanation: Luke 13:29-30 teaches that people from all nations will enter the kingdom and that traditional social rankings will be reversed, highlighting God's sovereign justice.
